title: Reclaimed & Junk Loose Parts
strapline: Bottle tops, cardboard tubes, keys and cotton reels — the rescued bits of everyday life, ready to become anything.
intent: Children think creatively and symbolically with genuinely open-ended, cost-free materials.
Children sort, classify and pattern with a huge variety of colours, sizes and textures.
Children build, connect and construct, solving how reclaimed parts fit and balance together.
Children develop early ideas about waste, reuse and caring for the planet.
Children own their creations completely, with no right answer and nothing to break.
implementation: Gather clean, safe reclaimed materials — bottle tops, tubes, corks, reels, keys, buttons, off-cuts — sorted into clear tubs.
Present them beautifully despite their humble origins — sorted by colour or type, they invite pattern and choice.
Follow the child's meaning: a stack of lids is a birthday cake, a tube is a telescope, the child decides.
Offer joining tools — tape, string, split pins, boxes — so parts can be connected and constructed.
Talk about where the materials came from and why we're giving them a new life instead of binning them.
Photograph and display the makes, and keep a 'parts we need' list for families to contribute to.
Rotate and refresh the collection so there's always something new to discover.
key_questions: What could this bottle top become in your game?
How will you join those two pieces together?
How did you decide which ones go in this tub?
This was going to be thrown away — what have you turned it into?
What comes next in the pattern you're making?

impact.text: Children use open-ended reclaimed parts symbolically, standing them in for anything in play.
Children sort and classify a huge variety of materials by their own rules.
Children build, connect and construct, solving how the parts fit and balance.
Children make and extend patterns with colourful, varied loose parts.
Children talk about reuse and caring for the planet, giving materials a new life.
Children choose, combine and adapt their materials and own the result with pride.
Children handle small parts and joining tools with growing precision.

enhancements: Clear tubs of sorted reclaimed parts — lids, tubes, corks, reels, keys, buttons.
Joining kit: masking tape, string, split pins, elastic bands and boxes.
A 'tinker tray' for laying out precise small arrangements.
A display shelf and camera to honour the finished makes.
A 'parts we need' list for families to fill from home recycling.
Wheels, axles and off-cuts for building things that move.
Mirrors and frames to turn arrangements into transient art.

playing_exploring: Nothing is precious, so children experiment boldly and take real risks with their ideas.
The same tub of lids becomes cakes, coins, wheels and counters across a week.
active_learning: Children set their own build goals and stick with them, adapting when parts won't hold.
There's no finished picture to match, so children decide for themselves when it's done.
creating_thinking: Reusing a 'rubbish' object as something new is inventive, flexible thinking.
Children solve how to join, balance and connect parts that were never designed to fit.
